# #21 Upsert by key — blind adversarial QA

Verdict: **PASS** for #21. No blocker or major defect was found in #21. One pre-existing major defect affects how #21 is used (D1).

How it was run: I did not read the implementation diff. I started a throwaway backend and vite with `scripts/lib/stack.sh` (`.verify/qa/21/hold.sh`; `FRONTEND_URL=http://fe.example`). The drivers live in `.verify/qa/21/`:
- REST: `rest1.mjs` to `rest6.mjs`, which write to SQLite to set up expired and legacy docs.
- MCP: `mcp.mjs` and `mcp2.mjs`. They use the SDK Client over stdio against `mcp-server.js`, and over StreamableHTTP against `mcp-server-http.js` on its own port.
- CLI: `cli.sh`.
- Chromium: `ui*.mjs`, run through `scripts/lib/browser-slot.sh`.

For a baseline I extracted `git archive HEAD` into the scratchpad and ran it on a second vite against the same backend. I tore everything down afterwards and never touched ports 3100, 3200 or 58747.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-21.1 PASS. 201 with created/changed true, 32-hex revision, editToken and editUrl. `url` = `http://fe.example/d/test-weekly`. ETag equals the revision.
- AC-21.2 PASS. 200 with created:false; same id, slug and url; new revision. `/revisions` has 2 entries and the last one has `note:"run 2"`.
- AC-21.3 PASS (stronger check). Two upserts by the same author milliseconds apart, rather than 10 s, still gave separate revisions. 20 parallel authorised updates gave 21 revisions, 20 notes and 20 distinct hashes.
- AC-21.4 PASS. Identical content returns 200 with changed:false, and the count stays the same.
- AC-21.5 PASS. No token gives 401 `edit_token_required`. A wrong token gives 403 `edit_token_invalid`. Bearer and X-Edit-Token disagreeing gives 403 (00 §9). Content is unchanged.
- AC-21.6 PASS. `Test`, `-x`, `a%20b`, `a%2Fb`, 129 chars, `.a`, `a%00b` and `%C3%A9t%C3%A9` all return 400 `invalid_key`. 128 chars, `a_b` and `a..b` are accepted. A raw `a/b` returns a 404 because the route does not match, which is acceptable.
- AC-21.7 PASS. A stale If-Match, or a stale `base_hash`, returns 412 with `content_hash` and `markdown`, the same shape as the `PUT /markdown` 412. A fresh If-Match returns 200.
- AC-21.8 PASS. On an expired doc, `GET /paste/:id` gives 410 and `GET by-key` gives 200 with `expired:true`. After an upsert, `GET` is 200 again with expiry at now+30.0 d. An expired doc with identical content is also revived (200 changed:false). `expiry_days:7` on update recomputes the expiry from now. When `expiry_days` is absent on a live doc, the expiry is unchanged. A never-expiring doc stays never-expiring.
- AC-21.9 PASS. Delete gives 204, then `GET by-key` gives 404. A re-upsert gives 201 with a new id, a new token and the reused slug `qa-del-slug`. The old token gets 403 on the new doc.
- AC-21.10 PASS. 10 two-way races each gave 201 + 401 with 1 row. 3 bursts of 20 each gave one 201, 19 × 401 and 1 row.
- AC-21.11 PASS on both servers. Each server has the exact spec description. A second connection without a token gets created:false with the same url. The store file has mode 600. Revisions carry by=`agent` and client=`mcp`. `list_revisions` shows `note`.
- AC-21.12 PASS. `revision-note` shows the note text only on the entries that have one, on desktop, on phone (390) and in dark mode. An HTML or script note renders as literal text: no `img`, `script` or `strong` element appears and the `onerror` did not fire. A 500-char unicode note wraps with no overflow. Screenshots: `.verify/qa/21/ui-desktop.png`, `ui-phone.png`, `ui-dark.png`.
- AC-21.13 PASS. An unknown key returns 404 and a known key returns 200 with the current revision. An invalid key on GET returns 400.

## Spec edge cases and my own
All of these passed:
- Key `cafe` while slug `cafe` exists: the key gets slug `cafe-2` and the other doc is untouched.
- A key equal to another doc's id creates a separate doc.
- A taken `slug` on create gives `cafe-3`, and the response shows the real slug.
- Slug on update is ignored.
- Reserved slugs: the keys `by-key`, `list`, slug `by-key`, sessionName `list` and slug `LIST` all get a suffix.
- Switching contentType from html to markdown stores and renders the new type. Leaving it out keeps the current one.
- Upsert followed by `PUT /markdown` with the old hash returns 412.
- When an upsert and a `PUT /markdown` with the same base run in parallel, exactly one wins and the other gets 412.
- Comments are kept across upserts.
- Percent-encoded `qa%3Arace` resolves to the same doc.
- A full-width unicode key returns 400.
- A query string on the URL is ignored.
- `changeNote` handling:
  - 501 chars returns 400.
  - 500 chars, or 500 chars with surrounding spaces, is trimmed and accepted.
  - A whitespace-only note is stored as absent.
  - A number returns 400.
  - Unicode, including NUL, is returned verbatim.
  - `GET /revisions/:hash` gives `note:null` when there is no note.
- A note given on create is stored on the first revision.
- A legacy doc (no token hash) can be upserted without a token, the same as `PUT /markdown`.
- A 20 MB body is created. A 51 MB body gets ECONNRESET, the same as `POST /paste` today.
- Bad JSON, missing markdown and a non-string markdown each return 400.
- A bogus `mode` returns 400.
- CLI `publish`:
  - Create prints url, revision and created.
  - No token: 401 with a hint and exit 1. A wrong token gives 403 and exit 1.
  - `--token` and `MDREVIEW_EDIT_TOKEN` both work, and `--note` is stored.
  - Identical content gives changed:false.
  - A 20 MB file works, a unicode file works, bad usage exits 1, and `--help` documents the command.
- MCP:
  - Content over 10 MB is rejected with a message pointing to the CLI and `create_via_shell`.
  - A doc created elsewhere returns 401 with guidance, and works when `editToken` is passed as an argument.
  - A wrong `editToken` argument returns 403 and does not overwrite the stored token: the next call without a token succeeds.

## Defects
- **D1, major, pre-existing, also on HEAD.** On a shared doc with no `filename`, DocHeader throws during render ("Unhandled error during execution of render function at <DocHeader>"). The header loses `doc-updated` and `menu-history`, so the revisions modal, and therefore the AC-21.12 note, cannot be reached.
  - Upserts made through REST or MCP without `filename` hit this. The CLI sets a filename, so it does not.
  - Repro: `PUT /paste/by-key/x:y {"markdown":"a"}`, open `/d/x-y`, open ☰. Only "Open file…" is shown (`.verify/qa/21/dbg.png`).
  - The same thing happens on the `git archive HEAD` baseline (`ui-base.mjs`), so #21 did not cause it. Fix it, or default `filename` on upsert create.
- **D2, minor.** An upsert that changes only meta (same markdown, new `sessionName`) returns `changed:true` but adds no revision. Rule 4 says a change is "always recorded as a new revision". This is arguably correct because the content hash is unchanged, but the spec does not settle it. Record a decision.
- **D3, minor.** An invalid `expiry_days` (0, -1, "abc", 3.5, 100000, "none") on update silently resets the expiry to 30 days instead of returning 400 or leaving it alone. This matches `POST /paste` create semantics. Only `null` means never.
- **D4, minor (inconsistency).** Upsert rejects `contentType:"text/html"` with 400 (it only allows `markdown|html`), while `POST /paste` stores `text/html` verbatim. Rule 3 says create "behaves like POST /paste".
- **D5, cosmetic.** MCP `upsert_session` errors leave out `code` for an invalid key (`{"error":"Invalid key","status":400}`); REST includes `invalid_key`. MCP errors come back with `isError:false`, which matches the existing tools.
- **D6, cosmetic, pre-existing.** At 390 px the revisions modal crushes the diff pane to 65 px (the baseline is the same, `phone-base.png`). A 500-char note makes its entry about 18 lines tall because there is no clamp.
